children.text: Put Pokémon in your party to climb.
Selecting this tower creates or updates your lobby. Review the mode, your party and invitations there before starting.
Pick a tower in the Hall and open a lobby. A tower is a climb of floors; each floor is a battle against wild opponents, then a boss.
Floors 5 and 10 are milestones with bigger bosses. Some towers keep going into harder cycles (Ascension).

You need a Tower Key (Rental Key for a rental draft; each player's first ordinary run of the day is free) and a registered party of up to six Pokemon. Invite friends in the lobby and everyone readies up.
In Rental Draft mode you borrow a team instead, and your own Pokemon stay safe.

At the intermission the team drafts a modifier (a harder floor for better rewards), can visit the vendor to heal or buy, and sometimes meets a room: Rest, Shrine, Forge, Library, Vault or Mystic Pool.
Relics from bosses and rooms help for the rest of the run (up to six). The team votes to keep climbing or cash out.
Rewards are banked at milestone floors, when you cash out and when you finish the tower. Cashing out keeps what is banked and ends the run.
Each day and week has its own tower, built from a mix of regions with its own rules. Everyone gets the same one.
You get one scored attempt on each trial; later runs are practice. Daily trials build a streak, and weekly trials add a rule for the whole week.
Achievements in a tower raise your mastery level there. The icon and number beside your name show your best tower.
Pick which tower shows, or hide it, in the Hall settings.
Talk to the Tower Keeper to open the Hall. /tower help shows this guide in chat. /tower report <text> tells us about a problem or an idea.
Reduced motion keeps every choice available.
Game volume stays in Minecraft's sound settings; the tower pages make no sounds of their own. Tower keys are set in Minecraft's controls screen, under Miscellaneous.
